fixes.explanation: That's exactly what they say. The lords rejoice and say, "Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands." They are praising Dagon, their god, for putting Samson in their hands. I think the whole room felt like they'd won the big game.

Nope, rain isn't what they say their god did. The lords gather to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon, and they say, "Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands." Their celebration is about Samson, friend.
Close, but that's not the word they use. The Philistines say, "Call for Samson to entertain us." The word is entertain, and they say it while their hearts are merry.
That's the one. The text says, "And they stationed him between the pillars." Remember that word, because those pillars are about to matter a lot.
Not quite. Samson asks to be led where he can "…feel the pillars supporting the temple, so I can lean against them." He wants to touch them and lean on them. Hiding isn't in his words.

Good thinking, but the crowd doesn't come up in what he asks. He says, "Lead me where I can feel the pillars supporting the temple, so I can lean against them." The reason he gives is to lean on the pillars.

His prayer isn't about shackles. He asks for strength so that "…with one vengeful blow I may pay back the Philistines for my two eyes." The blow is for paying back the Philistines, and shackles never come up in his prayer.

Not what he asks. Samson prays that "…with one vengeful blow I may pay back the Philistines for my two eyes." There's no mention of home in his prayer. His family does come for him and bury him later (Judges 16:31).
That's not what he says. He braces himself against the two pillars and says, "Let me die with the Philistines." Resting isn't in his words. It's a heavy line.

The temple doesn't just shake. The text says Samson "…pushed with all his might, and the temple fell on the lords and all the people in it." It comes down. Earlier he had asked the LORD to strengthen him just once more.

The text says otherwise. Samson's brothers and his father's family "…came down, carried him back…" and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. Gaza isn't the burial place the text names.
